newsitem.title: UK: Howard odds slip in UK Conservative leadership race.
newsitem.headline: Howard odds slip in UK Conservative leadership race.

text.p: Former home secretary Michael Howard's odds of winning the British Conservative Party leadership race have lengthened after he came under attack from a former colleague, bookmaker William Hill said on Tuesday.

Hill made Howard fourth favourite at 13-2, after having quoted him at 11-2 before former prisons minister Anne Widdecombe accused him of misleading parliament over a 1995 prison service crisis. Howard denies the allegation.
Favourite to succeed John Major as leader of the defeated Conservatives is still former Welsh secretary William Hague, on 8-13.
William Hill also offered former finance minister Kenneth Clarke and former social security secretary Peter Lilley at 5-1.
Arch anti-European John Redwood was quoted at 9-1, with former health secretary Stephen Dorrell at 14-1. --London Newsroom +44-171-542-7947
